Our lesson today is the beginning of Surah al-Nazi'at.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾

﴿By those who drag forth with violence (1), and those who draw out gently (2), and those who glide swiftly (3), and those who race forward (4), and those who arrange affairs (5)﴾ [al-Nazi'at 1-5].

The basmalah is a verse of the Book of Allah in its own right. It does not follow the surah before it or the one after it. For this reason, the more correct opinion is that the basmalah is not part of al-Fatihah but stands on its own. The evidence for this is the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, authentic in the two Sahihs, in which Allah says: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has praised Me." [[Narrated by Muslim (395/38) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

It is also not a verse of the other surahs. What we see in the Mushaf, where it is counted as a verse at the beginning of al-Fatihah alone, follows the view of some scholars. The correct position, however, is what I have mentioned to you: that it is a separate verse. For this reason, if a person in his prayer recites only ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah 2] through to the end of the surah, his prayer is still valid.

However, it is not found at the beginning of Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah). The reason is that the verse of the basmalah was not sent down to the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, between the two surahs, so it was not present there.

As for the reasoning of some scholars that Bara'ah was revealed with the sword, and so the basmalah was omitted, this is a defective reasoning that is not sound, because the sword, when it is used rightfully, is a truth and causes no harm.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ ﴿By those who drag forth with violence (1), and those who draw out gently (2), and those who glide swiftly (3), and those who race forward (4), and those who arrange affairs﴾. All these descriptions are for the angels, according to their deeds which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded them. So His saying ﴿By those who drag forth with violence﴾ means the angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the disbelievers; they drag them out ﴿with violence﴾, that is, they pull them out forcefully.

﴿And those who draw out gently﴾ means the angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the believers; they draw them out gently, that is, they extract them smoothly, like the al-unshutah (a slipknot). I think you know the unshutah: the knot that we call (al-takkah) here, or something similar in words, meaning a knot such that when you pull one of its ends the knot comes undone; it loosens quickly and easily.

So these angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the believers draw them out gently, that is, they extract them smoothly. The reason is that when the angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the disbelievers come to call the soul out, they address it with the most hideous descriptions. The angels say to the soul of the disbeliever: "Come out, you foul soul, who were in a foul body. Come out to the wrath of Allah," and similar words. So the soul recoils, does not wish to come out to this, and scatters within the body, may Allah protect us, until they seize it forcefully and tear it out, so that the body almost tears apart from the severity of the extraction.

As for the souls of the believers, may Allah make us and you among them, when the angels descend to seize them, they give them glad tidings: "Come out, you good soul, who were in a good body. Come out to the pleasure of Allah," and similar words that make it easy for the soul to part from the body it had grown accustomed to, so it leaves with ease.

This is why, when the Prophet, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him, said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'A'ishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not that, but the believer" — that is, when his appointed time comes — "is given glad tidings of mercy from Allah and His pleasure, so he loves to meet Allah." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6507) from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and Muslim (2684/15) from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them.]] Because at that moment he sees that he will move to a home better than the one he is leaving, so he rejoices, just as one of us rejoices when he is told: "Leave the house of mud for a house of plastered and lofty palaces, good," so he rejoices and loves to meet Allah.

The disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is the opposite. When he is given glad tidings of wrath and punishment, he dislikes to die; he dislikes to meet Allah, so Allah dislikes to meet him.

So then, ﴿By those who drag forth with violence﴾ — who are they? They are the angels who drag out the souls of the disbelievers, dragging them forcefully. ﴿And those who draw out gently﴾: the angels who seize the souls of the believers with ease and facility.

﴿And those who race forward﴾ also refers to the angels, who hasten to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the angels are swifter to the command of Allah and more upright in carrying out His command than the children of Adam. Allah, Exalted is He, said describing the angels of the Fire: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim 6]. And the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And those who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire (19). They glorify Him night and day, never slackening﴾ [al-Anbiya' 19-20]. They are thus swift to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whatever He commands them; they do not disobey Him in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded, because of their strength and their capacity to carry out the commands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And those who glide swiftly﴾ also refers to the angels, who glide by the command of Allah, that is, they hasten in it as a swimmer hastens in water. And as Allah, Exalted is He, said about the sun, the moon, the night and the day: ﴿Each in an orbit is gliding along﴾ [al-Anbiya' 33]. The meaning is that they glide by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, according to what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, willed. They — that is, the angels — are stronger than the jinn, and the jinn are stronger than human beings. Consider His saying, Exalted is He, about Solomon: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ (38) ﴿A stronger one among the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ (39) ﴿One who had knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾ [al-Naml 38-40]. That is, before you extend your gaze and then bring it back, I will bring it to you. ﴿And when he saw it placed beside him﴾ [al-Naml 40], at once he saw it, ﴿he said: This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml 40]. The scholars said: the angels carried it until they brought it to Solomon, from where? From Yemen, while Solomon was in al-Sham, in a moment. This shows that the strength of the angels is far greater than the strength of the jinn, and the strength of the jinn is greater than that of the children of Adam, because no human being can bring the throne of the queen of Sheba from Yemen to the north in a long period of time.

The conclusion is that the angels glide by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whatever He commands them.

﴿And those who arrange affairs﴾ is also a description of the angels who arrange the affair; the word is singular for "affairs." That is, the affairs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, have angels who manage them. Consider Jibril, who is entrusted with the revelation, receiving it from Allah and descending with it to the messengers. Israfil is entrusted with blowing the Trumpet on the Day of Resurrection: he blows the Trumpet and people are struck with terror and die, then he blows it again and they are raised. He is also among the bearers of the Throne. Mika'il is entrusted with rain and plants, with the rain and the vegetation. The Angel of Death is entrusted with the souls. Malik is entrusted with the Fire. Ridwan is entrusted with Paradise. On the right and on the left, the two watchers are entrusted with deeds. Each one manages what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded him, ﴿and those who arrange affairs﴾.

So then, to whom do all these descriptions belong? These descriptions belong to the angels according to their deeds. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, swore by the angels because they are among the best of creation, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, does not swear by anything except that it has a great standing, either in its own essence or because it is one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day the quaking one quakes (6), followed by the one that follows﴾ [al-Nazi'at 6-7]. Here ﴿On the Day﴾ is connected to an omitted element, and the implied meaning is: "Mention, O Muhammad, and remind the people of this great Day," ﴿the quaking one quakes (6), followed by the one that follows﴾. These are the two blasts of the Trumpet. With the first blast, people are shaken and terrified, then they all die except whom Allah wills. With the second blast, they are raised from their graves; people rise from their graves all at once. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It will be but one shout (13), and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13-14].

When the quaking one quakes and the one that follows follows it, people divide into two groups: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling (8), their eyes humbled﴾ [al-Nazi'at 8-9]. These are the hearts of the disbelievers. ﴿Trembling﴾ means fearful with intense fear.

﴿Their eyes humbled﴾ means abased; they can hardly look up or gaze steadily, rather their eyes are lowered, may Allah protect us, from their humiliation. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And you will see them being exposed to it, humbled by abasement, looking with sidelong glances﴾ [al-Shura 45].

We ask Allah, Exalted is He, to take care of us and of you in this world and the Hereafter, to make us among those who were saved on that Day from the punishment of Allah, to make us among His friends, the God-fearing, and His party, the successful. Indeed He is Most Generous, Most Noble.

I think you know the unshutah: the knot that we call (al-takkah) here, or something similar in words, meaning a knot such that when you pull one of its ends the knot comes undone; it loosens quickly and easily.

So these angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the believers draw them out gently, that is, they extract them smoothly. The reason is that when the angels entrusted with seizing the souls of the disbelievers come to call the soul out, they address it with the most hideous descriptions. The angels say to the soul of the disbeliever: "Come out, you foul soul, who were in a foul body. Come out to the wrath of Allah," and similar words. So the soul recoils, does not wish to come out to this, and scatters within the body, may Allah protect us, until they seize it forcefully and tear it out, so that the body almost tears apart from the severity of the extraction.

As for the souls of the believers, may Allah make us and you among them, when the angels descend to seize them, they give them glad tidings: "Come out, you good soul, who were in a good body. Come out to the pleasure of Allah," and similar words that make it easy for the soul to part from the body it had grown accustomed to, so it leaves with ease.

This is why, when the Prophet, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him, said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'A'ishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not that, but the believer" — that is, when his appointed time comes — "is given glad tidings of mercy from Allah and His pleasure, so he loves to meet Allah." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6507) from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and Muslim (2684/15) from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them.]] Because at that moment he sees that he will move to a home better than the one he is leaving, so he rejoices, just as one of us rejoices when he is told: "Leave the house of mud for a house of plastered and lofty palaces, good," so he rejoices and loves to meet Allah.

The disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is the opposite. When he is given glad tidings of wrath and punishment, he dislikes to die; he dislikes to meet Allah, so Allah dislikes to meet him.

So then, ﴿By those who drag forth with violence﴾ — who are they? They are the angels who drag out the souls of the disbelievers, dragging them forcefully. ﴿And those who draw out gently﴾: the angels who seize the souls of the believers with ease and facility.

﴿And those who race forward﴾ also refers to the angels, who hasten to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the angels are swifter to the command of Allah and more upright in carrying out His command than the children of Adam. Allah, Exalted is He, said describing the angels of the Fire: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim 6]. And the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And those who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire (19). They glorify Him night and day, never slackening﴾ [al-Anbiya' 19-20]. They are thus swift to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whatever He commands them; they do not disobey Him in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded, because of their strength and their capacity to carry out the commands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And those who glide swiftly﴾ also refers to the angels, who glide by the command of Allah, that is, they hasten in it as a swimmer hastens in water. And as Allah, Exalted is He, said about the sun, the moon, the night and the day: ﴿Each in an orbit is gliding along﴾ [al-Anbiya' 33]. The meaning is that they glide by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, according to what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, willed. They — that is, the angels — are stronger than the jinn, and the jinn are stronger than human beings. Consider His saying, Exalted is He, about Solomon: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ (38) ﴿A stronger one among the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ (39) ﴿One who had knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾ [al-Naml 38-40]. That is, before you extend your gaze and then bring it back, I will bring it to you. ﴿And when he saw it placed beside him﴾ [al-Naml 40], at once he saw it, ﴿he said: This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml 40]. The scholars said: the angels carried it until they brought it to Solomon, from where? From Yemen, while Solomon was in al-Sham, in a moment. This shows that the strength of the angels is far greater than the strength of the jinn, and the strength of the jinn is greater than that of the children of Adam, because no human being can bring the throne of the queen of Sheba from Yemen to the north in a long period of time.

The conclusion is that the angels glide by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whatever He commands them.

﴿And those who arrange affairs﴾ is also a description of the angels who arrange the affair; the word is singular for "affairs." That is, the affairs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, have angels who manage them. Consider Jibril, who is entrusted with the revelation, receiving it from Allah and descending with it to the messengers. Israfil is entrusted with blowing the Trumpet on the Day of Resurrection: he blows the Trumpet and people are struck with terror and die, then he blows it again and they are raised. He is also among the bearers of the Throne. Mika'il is entrusted with rain and plants, with the rain and the vegetation. The Angel of Death is entrusted with the souls. Malik is entrusted with the Fire. Ridwan is entrusted with Paradise. On the right and on the left, the two watchers are entrusted with deeds. Each one manages what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded him, ﴿and those who arrange affairs﴾.

So then, to whom do all these descriptions belong? These descriptions belong to the angels according to their deeds. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, swore by the angels because they are among the best of creation, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, does not swear by anything except that it has a great standing, either in its own essence or because it is one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day the quaking one quakes (6), followed by the one that follows﴾ [al-Nazi'at 6-7]. Here ﴿On the Day﴾ is connected to an omitted element, and the implied meaning is: "Mention, O Muhammad, and remind the people of this great Day," ﴿the quaking one quakes (6), followed by the one that follows﴾. These are the two blasts of the Trumpet. With the first blast, people are shaken and terrified, then they all die except whom Allah wills. With the second blast, they are raised from their graves; people rise from their graves all at once. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It will be but one shout (13), and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13-14].

When the quaking one quakes and the one that follows follows it, people divide into two groups: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling (8), their eyes humbled﴾ [al-Nazi'at 8-9]. These are the hearts of the disbelievers. ﴿Trembling﴾ means fearful with intense fear.

﴿Their eyes humbled﴾ means abased; they can hardly look up or gaze steadily, rather their eyes are lowered, may Allah protect us, from their humiliation. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And you will see them being exposed to it, humbled by abasement, looking with sidelong glances﴾ [al-Shura 45].

We ask Allah, Exalted is He, to take care of us and of you in this world and the Hereafter, to make us among those who were saved on that Day from the punishment of Allah, to make us among His friends, the God-fearing, and His party, the successful. Indeed He is Most Generous, Most Noble.

This meeting we begin with what we have reached in the tafsir of Surah an-Nazi'at.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said, explaining the establishment of the Hour: ﴿Then it will be but one shout (13), and they will be [instantly] on the surface of the earth.﴾ It is a shout from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by which they are driven and called out, and they rise from their graves standing as one man upon the surface of the earth after they had been in its depths. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us.﴾ [Ya-Sin 53].

In this one utterance, all of creation will come out of their graves alive, and then they will be brought before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to be recompensed. Therefore He said: ﴿Then it will be but one shout (13), and they will be [instantly] on the surface of the earth.﴾ This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.﴾ [al-Qamar 50]. That is, the command of Allah, when He wills something to be, is only one [word]: "Be" (kun), and this does not delay by a moment from Allah's word, ﴿but one, like a glance of the eye.﴾ Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not incapable of anything. So if all creatures rise from their graves to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by a single word, this is the strongest proof that Allah is capable of all things, and that nothing in the heavens or on the earth can overpower Him, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is not one to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing and Competent.﴾ [Fatir 44].

﴿Then it will be but one shout (13), and they will be [instantly] on the surface of the earth.﴾ Then Allah, exalted is He, said, explaining what happened to the nations before Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

It should be known that Allah's narrating to us the accounts of the nations before him has many benefits and great lessons, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly there is in their stories a lesson for people of understanding.﴾ [Yusuf 111].

* Among these is the consolation of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, for what he suffered from his people of harm in word and deed. It is as if Allah is saying to him: The messengers before you were also harmed. ﴿And messengers before you were denied, and they endured patiently what they were denied and harmed, until Our help reached them. None can alter the words of Allah. And there has already come to you some of the news of the messengers.﴾ [al-An'am 34].

* Among these is that it contains a warning to those who deny the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that there may befall them what befell the earlier nations of punishment and retribution. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is the like thereof.﴾ [Muhammad 10].

And the lessons in the narratives, the narratives of the prophets, are many.

Allah said: ﴿Has there reached you the story of Musa?﴾ [an-Nazi'at 15]. The address in His saying ﴿Has there reached you﴾ is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, or to everyone to whom address is directed and for whom it is valid. According to the first meaning: ﴿Has there reached you﴾ O Muhammad; according to the second meaning: ﴿Has there reached you﴾ O human being.

﴿The story of Musa﴾: he is the son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, the best of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and one of the five Ulu al-'Azm (resolute messengers), who are: Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Nuh. These five are mentioned in the Qur'an in two places. One is in al-Ahzab, in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ahzab 7]. The second is in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa﴾ [ash-Shura 13].

The story of Musa, peace be upon him, is mentioned in the Qur'an more than others, because Musa is the prophet of the Jews, who were numerous in Medina and around it during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore the stories of Musa were the most narrated to us of the news of the prophets, and the most comprehensive and extensive.

In His saying ﴿Has there reached you the story of Musa﴾ there is an arousing of the listener's interest to hear what happened in this story.

﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa﴾ [an-Nazi'at 16]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, called to him with a call that he heard with the voice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah said: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mount and brought him near as one confiding.﴾ [Maryam 52]. ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa (16), Go to Pharaoh﴾ [an-Nazi'at 16–17]. Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, and he used to say to his people that he was their most high lord, and that there was no god other than him. He said: ﴿O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than myself.﴾ [al-Qasas 38]. So he claimed what was not his, and denied the right of another, namely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿the sacred valley﴾ refers to Tuwa, and the valley is the course of water; Allah named it sacred because revelation came to Musa, peace be upon him, there.

His saying ﴿Tuwa﴾ is the name of the valley.

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed (17). And say, "Would you like to purify yourself?"﴾ [an-Nazi'at 17–18].

The rest of the story will come, God willing, since time today was short, so we will limit ourselves to this. We ask Allah, may He make this a blessed and beneficial meeting.

This meeting we begin with what we have reached in the tafsir of Surah an-Nazi'at.

The address in His saying ﴿Has there reached you﴾ is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, or to everyone to whom address is directed and for whom it is valid. According to the first meaning: ﴿Has there reached you﴾ O Muhammad; according to the second meaning: ﴿Has there reached you﴾ O human being.

﴿The story of Musa﴾: he is the son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, the best of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and one of the five Ulu al-'Azm (resolute messengers), who are: Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Nuh. These five are mentioned in the Qur'an in two places. One is in al-Ahzab, in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ahzab 7]. The second is in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa﴾ [ash-Shura 13].

The story of Musa, peace be upon him, is mentioned in the Qur'an more than others, because Musa is the prophet of the Jews, who were numerous in Medina and around it during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore the stories of Musa were the most narrated to us of the news of the prophets, and the most comprehensive and extensive.

In His saying ﴿Has there reached you the story of Musa﴾ there is an arousing of the listener's interest to hear what happened in this story.

﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa﴾ [an-Nazi'at 16]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, called to him with a call that he heard with the voice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah said: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mount and brought him near as one confiding.﴾ [Maryam 52]. ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa (16), Go to Pharaoh﴾ [an-Nazi'at 16–17]. Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, and he used to say to his people that he was their most high lord, and that there was no god other than him. He said: ﴿O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than myself.﴾ [al-Qasas 38]. So he claimed what was not his, and denied the right of another, namely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿the sacred valley﴾ refers to Tuwa, and the valley is the course of water; Allah named it sacred because revelation came to Musa, peace be upon him, there.

His saying ﴿Tuwa﴾ is the name of the valley.

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed (17). And say, "Would you like to purify yourself?"﴾ [an-Nazi'at 17–18].

The rest of the story will come, God willing, since time today was short, so we will limit ourselves to this. We ask Allah, may He make this a blessed and beneficial meeting.

In our discussion today, or at the start of this meeting, we speak about the rest of the verses in Surah An-Nazi'at, at His saying, the Exalted, addressing Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed.﴾ So Allah commanded His Prophet Musa to go to Pharaoh, and this is the message. He explained the reason for that, which is the transgression of this man, meaning Pharaoh. In Surah Ta-Ha He said: ﴿Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed﴾ [Ta-Ha 43]. There is no contradiction between the two verses. Allah the Exalted first sent Musa, then Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to strengthen his back through his brother Harun, so Harun was sent with Musa, and Musa and Harun both became messengers to Pharaoh.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed he has transgressed﴾ means: he exceeded his limit, because tughyan (transgression) is excess. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its limit, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [Al-Haqqah 11]. ﴿Tagha﴾ means: it increased. From it comes at-taghut (the false object of worship), because in it there is transgression of the limit.

Here Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed he has transgressed. So say, "Would you like to purify yourself?"﴾. The interrogative here is for encouragement, encouraging Pharaoh to purify himself from the evil and corruption he is upon. The origin of zakah is growth and increase, and it is used in the sense of Islam and monotheism. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ [Fussilat 6-7]. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who instills it [with corruption]﴾ [Ash-Shams 9-10].

﴿"Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear [Him]"﴾ [An-Nazi'at 18-19]: that is, I would direct you to your Lord, that is, to the religion of Allah, mighty and majestic, which leads to Allah.

﴿So you would fear﴾ means: you would fear Allah, mighty and majestic, with knowledge on your part, because khashyah (fear accompanied by knowledge) is fear combined with knowledge. If there is no knowledge, it is mere fear. This is the difference between khashyah and khawf: the khashyah is from knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28]. As for khawf, it is mere fright that occurs to a person even without knowledge. That is why a person may fear something he imagines; he may see in a dark night a shape that has no reality and fear it. That is fright based on delusion. But khashyah is from knowledge. ﴿And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear [Him].﴾

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾ [An-Nazi'at 20]: that is, Musa (peace be upon him) went and said to Pharaoh what Allah had commanded him, ﴿Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear [Him].﴾ Since people do not believe or accept a person's claim to be a messenger except with a sign, just as it is evident that a person does not accept any claim from anyone except with evidence, Allah, glorified and exalted, placed with every messenger a sign that indicates his truthfulness. Here He said: ﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾, meaning: Musa showed Pharaoh the greatest sign. What is this sign? The sign was that he had a staff of wood from the branches of a tree, as is well known. When he placed it on the ground, it became a moving serpent; then he took it up and it returned to being a staff. This is one of the signs of Allah: that an inanimate thing, when placed on the ground, becomes a moving serpent, and when taken up from the ground, it immediately returns to its original state, which is a staff among staffs.

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign.﴾ The Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent with this sign, and with his putting his hand into his collar and it coming out white without harm, that is, without defect: white with a whiteness that is not the whiteness of vitiligo, but a whiteness that Allah made a sign. Allah sent him with that, with the staff and the hand, because at the time of Musa, magic was widespread and common. So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent him with something resembling magic, but it is not magic in reality, in order to overcome the magicians who confronted Musa (peace be upon him).

The people of knowledge said: In the time of Isa (peace be upon him), medicine spread greatly, so Isa came with a matter that defeated the physicians. He would not touch anyone afflicted with an ailment, whatever ailment it was, except that he was healed. When someone with an ailment was brought to him, he would touch him with his hand and he would be healed by Allah's permission. He would heal the blind from birth (al-akmah) and the leper, even though leprosy has no cure, yet he would heal the leper by Allah's permission, and he would heal the one born without eyes. Greater than this and more significant, he would give life to the dead by Allah's permission: the dead would be brought to him, he would speak with him, and life would return to him. And more severe and more eloquent than that, he would bring out the dead by Allah's permission. From where would he bring them out? From their graves. He would stand at the grave and call to the one in it, and he would come out of the grave alive. This is something no medicine could ever reach. That is why the sign of Isa at that time was entirely suited to what the people were upon.

The people of knowledge said: As for the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (peace be upon him), he came to the Arabs, who boasted of eloquence and regarded eloquence as the greatest virtue of a person. So Muhammad (peace be upon him) came with this great Qur'an, which defeated the masters of eloquence, and they were unable to produce its like. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants."﴾ [Al-Isra' 88], meaning: even if some of them helped others, they would never produce its like.

At this point we say: Musa (peace be upon him) showed Pharaoh the greatest sign, but did Pharaoh benefit from the signs? No. ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101]. ﴿You can only warn one who follows the reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen﴾ [Ya-Sin 11]. Those in whose hearts there is no readiness for guidance will not be guided, even if every sign came to them, may Allah protect us. That is why He said: ﴿But he denied and disobeyed﴾ [An-Nazi'at 21]: he denied the report and disobeyed the command. That is, he said to Musa: "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad" [Ash-Shu'ara' 27], and he disobeyed the command. He did not comply with Musa's command and did not submit to his law.

﴿Then he turned his back, striving﴾ [An-Nazi'at 22]: ﴿turned his back﴾ means he withdrew, going about vigorously.

﴿Then he gathered [his people] and called out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 23]: he gathered the people, that is, assembled them, and called out to them in a raised voice, so that this would be more effective in forbidding them from what Musa (peace be upon him) wanted from them.

﴿Then he gathered [his people] and called out, and said, "I am your lord, the most high"﴾ [An-Nazi'at 23-24], may Allah protect us. He said to his people: "I am your lord, the most high," meaning there is no one above me, because "al-a'la" (the most high) is a superlative from elevation. Observe how this man became arrogant and claimed for himself what was not his in his saying: ﴿I am your lord, the most high.﴾ He boasted of the rivers and the vast kingdom, and he said to his people, among the many statements he made to them: ﴿O my people, is not mine the dominion of Egypt and these rivers flowing beneath me? Then do you not see? Or am I better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 51-52].

So what happened?

Allah, mighty and majestic, drowned him in the water he had boasted of, and Allah gave the kingdom of Egypt as an inheritance to the Children of Israel, whom he had oppressed.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾ [An-Nazi'at 25]. Allah seized him with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. ﴿The punishment of the Hereafter and the first﴾ means that He made him an example in the Hereafter and in this world. So he became a lesson in his own time and a lesson after his time until the Day of Resurrection. Everyone who reads the Book of Allah and what Allah did to Pharaoh takes it as a lesson to learn from: how Allah destroyed him despite this great kingdom, this tyranny, and this transgression, so that he became more insignificant before Allah than anything insignificant.

Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears [Allah]﴾ [An-Nazi'at 26]. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ means: in what occurred of Musa's being sent to Pharaoh, his dialogue with him, Pharaoh's contempt for him, and his arrogance in refusing to submit to him, there is a lesson. A lesson for whom? ﴿For whoever fears﴾, that is, fears Allah, mighty and majestic. Whoever has fear of Allah and reflects on what happened to Musa with Pharaoh, and the outcome that came to each of them, will take a lesson from it. The lessons in the story of Musa are many. If one of you were to volunteer to gather the story from the verses in every surah and then deduce the lessons that arise from this story, that would be good. Will any of you do that?

* Student: Let it be after some days, God willing.

* Shaykh: Yes, you have fifteen days. In any case, if we find someone before you, he has more right to it; otherwise it is yours. Whoever comes first is the one who precedes.

* Student: Gather the lessons, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: Yes, that is, he brings the whole story across all the verses, because some surahs contain things that others do not. If he gathers them and says, for example: "The following lessons are drawn from this great story," and then lists them. I do not necessarily mean the legal rulings of jurisprudence, because those may be lengthy. But the lessons: how Allah the Mighty sent them to Pharaoh, how He said to them: ﴿So speak to him with gentle speech﴾ [Ta-Ha 44] even though he was arrogant and wicked, and what the outcome was. How Musa (peace be upon him) left Egypt fearful for himself, watching and waiting, just as the Messenger (peace be upon him) left Makkah watching and waiting, and the final outcome was for the Messenger (peace be upon him) and for Musa. But the outcome for the Messenger came through the Messenger's own action and his companions' action, as Allah punished their enemies at their hands, while the outcome for Musa came through the action of Allah, mighty and majestic. The point is that a person draws lessons from this that he uses to reform himself and his heart, until the matter becomes clear. In any case, mentioning the words of the scholars is good, because the words of the scholars help in understanding the meaning. We stop at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the sky? He constructed it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 27]. I think we have discussed it, but there is no harm. In any case, that is fine; repetition is not objectionable when it is beneficial.

Here these words end, which I ask Allah, mighty and majestic, to make sincerely for Him and beneficial for all of us.

From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its limit, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [Al-Haqqah 11]. ﴿Tagha﴾ means: it increased. From it comes at-taghut (the false object of worship), because in it there is transgression of the limit.

The interrogative here is for encouragement, encouraging Pharaoh to purify himself from the evil and corruption he is upon. The origin of zakah is growth and increase, and it is used in the sense of Islam and monotheism. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ [Fussilat 6-7]. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who instills it [with corruption]﴾ [Ash-Shams 9-10].

﴿So you would fear﴾ means: you would fear Allah, mighty and majestic, with knowledge on your part, because khashyah (fear accompanied by knowledge) is fear combined with knowledge. If there is no knowledge, it is mere fear. This is the difference between khashyah and khawf: the khashyah is from knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28]. As for khawf, it is mere fright that occurs to a person even without knowledge. That is why a person may fear something he imagines; he may see in a dark night a shape that has no reality and fear it. That is fright based on delusion. But khashyah is from knowledge. ﴿And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear [Him].﴾

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾ [An-Nazi'at 20]: that is, Musa (peace be upon him) went and said to Pharaoh what Allah had commanded him, ﴿Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear [Him].﴾ Since people do not believe or accept a person's claim to be a messenger except with a sign, just as it is evident that a person does not accept any claim from anyone except with evidence, Allah, glorified and exalted, placed with every messenger a sign that indicates his truthfulness. Here He said: ﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾, meaning: Musa showed Pharaoh the greatest sign. What is this sign? The sign was that he had a staff of wood from the branches of a tree, as is well known. When he placed it on the ground, it became a moving serpent; then he took it up and it returned to being a staff. Allah sent him with that, with the staff and the hand, because at the time of Musa, magic was widespread and common. So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent him with something resembling magic, but it is not magic in reality, in order to overcome the magicians who confronted Musa (peace be upon him).

The people of knowledge said: In the time of Isa (peace be upon him), medicine spread greatly, so Isa came with a matter that defeated the physicians. He would not touch anyone afflicted with an ailment, whatever ailment it was, except that he was healed. When someone with an ailment was brought to him, he would touch him with his hand and he would be healed by Allah's permission. He would heal the blind from birth (al-akmah) and the leper, even though leprosy has no cure, yet he would heal the leper by Allah's permission, and he would heal the one born without eyes. Greater than this and more significant, he would give life to the dead by Allah's permission: the dead would be brought to him, he would speak with him, and life would return to him. And more severe and more eloquent than that, he would bring out the dead by Allah's permission. From where would he bring them out? From their graves. He would stand at the grave and call to the one in it, and he would come out of the grave alive. This is something no medicine could ever reach. That is why the sign of Isa at that time was entirely suited to what the people were upon.

The people of knowledge said: As for the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (peace be upon him), he came to the Arabs, who boasted of eloquence and regarded eloquence as the greatest virtue of a person. So Muhammad (peace be upon him) came with this great Qur'an, which defeated the masters of eloquence, and they were unable to produce its like. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants."﴾ [Al-Isra' 88], meaning: even if some of them helped others, they would never produce its like.

At this point we say: Musa (peace be upon him) showed Pharaoh the greatest sign, but did Pharaoh benefit from the signs? No. ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101]. ﴿You can only warn one who follows the reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen﴾ [Ya-Sin 11]. Those in whose hearts there is no readiness for guidance will not be guided, even if every sign came to them, may Allah protect us. That is why He said: ﴿But he denied and disobeyed﴾ [An-Nazi'at 21]: he denied the report and disobeyed the command. That is, he said to Musa: "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad" [Ash-Shu'ara' 27], and he disobeyed the command. He did not comply with Musa's command and did not submit to his law.

﴿Then he turned his back, striving﴾ [An-Nazi'at 22]: ﴿turned his back﴾ means he withdrew, going about vigorously.

﴿Then he gathered [his people] and called out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 23]: he gathered the people, that is, assembled them, and called out to them in a raised voice, so that this would be more effective in forbidding them from what Musa (peace be upon him) wanted from them.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 79, verses 27–46 (part 1 of 2)**

Held every Thursday. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make these gatherings blessed. We begin this session with the explanation (tafsir) of verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We started from Surah An-Naba' and are proceeding to the end of the Qur'an. We are now at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He built it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 27–28], and so on to the end.

Allah, glorified and exalted, addresses His servants, saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾. By this interrogative He intends to establish that resurrection is possible, because the polytheists denied the Prophet ﷺ regarding resurrection and said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 78]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾

The answer is known to everyone: it is the heaven, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir 57].

﴿He built it﴾: this sentence is not connected to what precedes it. Therefore, when the reader recites, he should pause at His saying ﴿or is the heaven?﴾, then begin anew with ﴿He built it﴾. The sentence is resumptive (istinafiyyah, a new sentence), to show the greatness of the heaven.

﴿He built it﴾ means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, built it. In another verse, in Surah Adh-Dhariyat, Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that He built it with power, as He said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength [bi-aydin], and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 47]. ﴿With strength﴾ means: with might.

﴿He raised its height and proportioned it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 28]: ﴿raised its height﴾ means: He raised it above the earth. He raised it, the Mighty and Majestic, without pillars, as He said: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you see﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 2].

﴿And proportioned it﴾ means: He made it level and made it complete and perfect, as He said regarding the creation of man: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you and proportioned you﴾ [Al-Infitar 6–7]. That is, He made you well-formed and of complete creation. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, proportioned the heaven.

﴿And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness﴾ [An-Nazi'at 29]: ﴿He darkened its night﴾ means: He made it dark, so the night is dark. Allah says: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra' 12].

﴿And extracted its brightness﴾: He explained it by the sun, which rises each day from its place of rising and sets in its place of setting.

﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 30]: ﴿after that﴾ means: after the creation of the heavens and the earth.

﴿He spread it out﴾, and He explained this spreading by His saying: ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾ [An-Nazi'at 31–32], ﴿as enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾ [An-Nazi'at 33]. The earth was created before the heaven, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed firmly on it mountains from above it, and blessed it, and determined in it its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat 9–12]. So the earth was created before the heaven, but its spreading out, the extraction of water from it, and its pasture came after the creation of the heavens.

﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾: that is, He made them fixed in the earth, holding the earth so that it would not shake with its creatures.

﴿As enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾: that is, Allah, exalted is He, made that as enjoyment for us, which we use for what we eat and drink, and for our livestock, that is, our animals: camels, cattle, sheep, and others.

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminded His servants of these blessings, which indicate the perfection of His power, He reminded them of their inevitable end, which none can avoid. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34]. That is the establishment of the Hour. He called it "catastrophe" (ṭāmmah) because it is a great calamity that overwhelms everything before it. "Greatest" (kubrā) means: greater than every other catastrophe.

﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes, the day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34–35] is an explanation of this day on which the greatest catastrophe will occur, and it is the day on which man will remember what he strove for. How will he remember it? He will remember it written down, recorded with him, which he himself will read. Allah says: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will encounter spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. When he reads it, he will remember what he strove for, that is, what he did. In this world we have forgotten what we did. We did many deeds, some righteous, some vain, and some evil, but we forget all of this. On the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to us in a book, and it will be said: "Read your record yourself." ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ Then he will remember what he strove for. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I had been dust."﴾ [An-Naba' 40].

Then He said: ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever can see﴾ [An-Nazi'at 36]. May Allah protect us and you from it. ﴿Brought forth﴾ means: made manifest. It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who will lead it. When the wrongdoers are thrown into a narrow place there, bound together, they will call out there for destruction [thubur]. It will come, may Allah protect us, to whoever sees and perceives, and hearts will be torn apart and the infant will turn gray.

For this reason He said: ﴿So as for he who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 37–39]. These are two attributes belonging to the people of the Fire: transgression, which is exceeding the limit, and preferring the life of this world over the Hereafter by giving it precedence over the Hereafter and making it the greatest concern of a person.

If someone asks: what is transgression? We say: transgression is exceeding the limit, as we mentioned just now. Exceeding the limit in what? What is man's limit? Man's limit is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. Whoever exceeds his limit and does not worship Allah, he is the transgressor. This is the transgressor, because he has overstepped the limit. You were not created to eat, enjoy yourself, and take pleasure as livestock do. You were created to worship Allah, so worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you do not, then you have transgressed. This is transgression: that a person does not worship Allah.

His saying ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ and the previous attribute are mutually connected. The one who transgresses against the worship of Allah prefers the worldly life, because he uses it as an excuse to abandon obedience to Allah and is distracted by it from obeying Allah. When the dawn call is made, he prefers sleep over prayer. When he is told to remember Allah, he prefers idle talk over the remembrance of Allah, and so on.

His saying ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ means: it will be his abode. "Refuge" (ma'wā) means the place of return and the dwelling. How wretched is the dwelling of Hellfire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40] means: he feared standing before Him, because on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will confront a person with his sins, and he will say: "I did such and such, I did such and such, I did such and such," as occurs in the authentic hadith. When he confesses, Allah will say to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you."[1] This is the one who feared this standing.

﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40]: that is, from its desires. The soul commands evil, and it commands only wrongdoing. But there is another soul opposed to it, the tranquil soul, because a human being has three souls: the tranquil soul, the commanding soul, and the self-reproaching soul, and all are mentioned in the Qur'an.

As for the tranquil soul, it is in His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise﴾ [Al-Fajr 27–30].

As for the commanding soul to evil, it is in His saying: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent commander of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

As for the self-reproaching soul, it is in His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 1–2].

A person senses these souls within himself. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward good, he loves good and does it; this is the tranquil soul. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward evil and does it; this is the commanding soul to evil. Then comes the self-reproaching soul, which blames him for what he did, so you find him regretting the sin he committed. Or there is another self-reproaching soul that blames him for doing good, may Allah protect us. Some people may blame themselves for doing good and for keeping company with the people of good, and say: "How can I keep company with these people who have turned me away from my life, my desires, my amusements, and the like?"

So the self-reproaching soul is a soul that sometimes blames the commanding soul to evil, and sometimes blames the tranquil soul. In reality it is a soul between two souls: it blames the commanding soul when it does evil and causes the person to feel remorse, and it may also blame the tranquil soul when it does good. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40–41]. Paradise is the abode of bliss which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is what the Qur'an says, and the sacred hadith says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[2] This Paradise a person may perceive before he dies. How? When the appointed time arrives and the angels call the soul to depart, they say: "Come out, O tranquil soul, to the pleasure of Allah," and the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [An-Nahl 32]. When do they say it? At the time of death.

So the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise, and its spirit departs content, easy, and smooth. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].

---

[1] Agreed upon (Bukhari 2441; Muslim 2768/52), narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[2] Agreed upon (Bukhari 3244; Muslim 2824/2), narrated from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.
[3] Narrated by al-Bukhari (6507) from 'Ubadah ibn as-Samit, and Muslim (2684/15) from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[4] Narrated in this wording by at-Tirmidhi (2385) from Anas. The hadith is agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3688) and Muslim (2639/161) narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, saying: "When is the Hour?" He said: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "Nothing, except that I love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ." He said: "You are with the one you love." Anas said: "We never rejoiced at anything as we rejoiced at the Prophet's ﷺ saying: 'You are with the one you love.'"

Jibril (may peace be upon him), who is the most knowledgeable of the messengers, asked the Prophet (ﷺ), who is the most knowledgeable of all mankind. He said: "Tell me about the Hour." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "The one who is asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the one who asks" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)]. That is, if it is hidden from you, then it is hidden from me as well. And if the most knowledgeable of the angels and the most knowledgeable of mankind do not know when the Hour will come, then what of those below them? From this we learn that what some people spread, that the Hour will occur on such-and-such a date or in such-and-such a time, is entirely false, and we know that they are liars in this, because they do not know when the Hour will come; none knows it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 45]. That is, you have no knowledge of it, but you are a warner. A warner of whom? ﴿Those who fear it﴾, that is, those who dread it, and they are the believers. As for those who deny it, consider it far-fetched and reject it, warning does not benefit them, ﴿and signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101].

So we say: you do not ask when you will die, nor where you will die, because this is a matter that does not need to be asked about; it is a settled matter, and it must happen. However long you remain in this world, it is as if you remained only a single day. Indeed, as Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46].

But the question that must come to the self, and for which you must have an answer, is: In what state will you die? By my saying "in what state," I do not mean whether you are rich or poor, strong or weak, with a family or childless. No, in what state will you die in terms of your deeds? This is the point.

If you ask yourself this question, you must prepare, you must prepare, because you do not know when death will surprise you. How many a person has gone out driving his car and was brought back carried on shoulders! How many a person has left his family saying, "Prepare lunch or dinner for me," but never ate it! How many a person has put on his shirt and buttoned its buttons, and none undid them except the one who washes him for burial! This is a matter witnessed in sudden accidents, in whatever state one may be.

Look now and think about the state in which you will die—we ask Allah to grant me and you repentance and turning back to Him. Therefore, you should increase your seeking of forgiveness, increase it as much as you can, for seeking forgiveness contains relief from every distress and a way out from every constriction. Some scholars even say: if a person asks you for a fatwa, seek Allah's forgiveness before you issue it, because sins come between a person and guidance. They derived this from the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 105, 106], ﴿that you may judge﴾, ﴿seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 106].

This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

If you do not, then you have transgressed. This is transgression: that a person does not worship Allah.

His saying ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ and the previous attribute are mutually connected. The one who transgresses against the worship of Allah prefers the worldly life, because he uses it as an excuse to abandon obedience to Allah and is distracted by it from obeying Allah. When the dawn call is made, he prefers sleep over prayer. When he is told to remember Allah, he prefers idle talk over the remembrance of Allah, and so on.

His saying ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ means: it will be his abode. "Refuge" (ma'wā) means the place of return and the dwelling. How wretched is the dwelling of Hellfire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40] means: he feared standing before Him, because on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will confront a person with his sins, and he will say: "I did such and such, I did such and such, I did such and such," as occurs in the authentic hadith. When he confesses, Allah will say to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you."[1] This is the one who feared this standing.

﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40]: that is, from its desires. The soul commands evil, and it commands only wrongdoing. But there is another soul opposed to it, the tranquil soul, because a human being has three souls: the tranquil soul, the commanding soul, and the self-reproaching soul, and all are mentioned in the Qur'an.

As for the tranquil soul, it is in His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise﴾ [Al-Fajr 27–30].

As for the commanding soul to evil, it is in His saying: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent commander of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

As for the self-reproaching soul, it is in His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 1–2].

A person senses these souls within himself. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward good, he loves good and does it; this is the tranquil soul. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward evil and does it; this is the commanding soul to evil. Then comes the self-reproaching soul, which blames him for what he did, so you find him regretting the sin he committed. Or there is another self-reproaching soul that blames him for doing good, may Allah protect us. Some people may blame themselves for doing good and for keeping company with the people of good, and say: "How can I keep company with these people who have turned me away from my life, my desires, my amusements, and the like?"

So the self-reproaching soul is a soul that sometimes blames the commanding soul to evil, and sometimes blames the tranquil soul. In reality it is a soul between two souls: it blames the commanding soul when it does evil and causes the person to feel remorse, and it may also blame the tranquil soul when it does good. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40–41]. Paradise is the abode of bliss which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is what the Qur'an says, and the sacred hadith says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[2] This Paradise a person may perceive before he dies. How? When the appointed time arrives and the angels call the soul to depart, they say: "Come out, O tranquil soul, to the pleasure of Allah," and the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [An-Nahl 32]. When do they say it? At the time of death.

So the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise, and its spirit departs content, easy, and smooth. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].
