This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 79, verses 27–46 (part 1 of 2)**

Held every Thursday. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make these gatherings blessed. We begin this session with the explanation (tafsir) of verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We started from Surah An-Naba' and are proceeding to the end of the Qur'an. We are now at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He built it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 27–28], and so on to the end.

Allah, glorified and exalted, addresses His servants, saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾. By this interrogative He intends to establish that resurrection is possible, because the polytheists denied the Prophet ﷺ regarding resurrection and said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 78]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾

The answer is known to everyone: it is the heaven, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir 57].

﴿He built it﴾: this sentence is not connected to what precedes it. Therefore, when the reader recites, he should pause at His saying ﴿or is the heaven?﴾, then begin anew with ﴿He built it﴾. The sentence is resumptive (istinafiyyah, a new sentence), to show the greatness of the heaven.

﴿He built it﴾ means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, built it. In another verse, in Surah Adh-Dhariyat, Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that He built it with power, as He said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength [bi-aydin], and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 47]. ﴿With strength﴾ means: with might.

﴿He raised its height and proportioned it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 28]: ﴿raised its height﴾ means: He raised it above the earth. He raised it, the Mighty and Majestic, without pillars, as He said: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you see﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 2].

﴿And proportioned it﴾ means: He made it level and made it complete and perfect, as He said regarding the creation of man: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you and proportioned you﴾ [Al-Infitar 6–7]. That is, He made you well-formed and of complete creation. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, proportioned the heaven.

﴿And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness﴾ [An-Nazi'at 29]: ﴿He darkened its night﴾ means: He made it dark, so the night is dark. Allah says: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra' 12].

﴿And extracted its brightness﴾: He explained it by the sun, which rises each day from its place of rising and sets in its place of setting.

﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 30]: ﴿after that﴾ means: after the creation of the heavens and the earth.

﴿He spread it out﴾, and He explained this spreading by His saying: ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾ [An-Nazi'at 31–32], ﴿as enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾ [An-Nazi'at 33]. The earth was created before the heaven, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed firmly on it mountains from above it, and blessed it, and determined in it its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat 9–12]. So the earth was created before the heaven, but its spreading out, the extraction of water from it, and its pasture came after the creation of the heavens.

﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾: that is, He made them fixed in the earth, holding the earth so that it would not shake with its creatures.

﴿As enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾: that is, Allah, exalted is He, made that as enjoyment for us, which we use for what we eat and drink, and for our livestock, that is, our animals: camels, cattle, sheep, and others.

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminded His servants of these blessings, which indicate the perfection of His power, He reminded them of their inevitable end, which none can avoid. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34]. That is the establishment of the Hour. He called it "catastrophe" (ṭāmmah) because it is a great calamity that overwhelms everything before it. "Greatest" (kubrā) means: greater than every other catastrophe.

﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes, the day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34–35] is an explanation of this day on which the greatest catastrophe will occur, and it is the day on which man will remember what he strove for. How will he remember it? He will remember it written down, recorded with him, which he himself will read. Allah says: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will encounter spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. When he reads it, he will remember what he strove for, that is, what he did. In this world we have forgotten what we did. We did many deeds, some righteous, some vain, and some evil, but we forget all of this. On the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to us in a book, and it will be said: "Read your record yourself." ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ Then he will remember what he strove for. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I had been dust."﴾ [An-Naba' 40].

Then He said: ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever can see﴾ [An-Nazi'at 36]. May Allah protect us and you from it. ﴿Brought forth﴾ means: made manifest. It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who will lead it. When the wrongdoers are thrown into a narrow place there, bound together, they will call out there for destruction [thubur]. It will come, may Allah protect us, to whoever sees and perceives, and hearts will be torn apart and the infant will turn gray.

For this reason He said: ﴿So as for he who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 37–39]. These are two attributes belonging to the people of the Fire: transgression, which is exceeding the limit, and preferring the life of this world over the Hereafter by giving it precedence over the Hereafter and making it the greatest concern of a person.

If someone asks: what is transgression? We say: transgression is exceeding the limit, as we mentioned just now. Exceeding the limit in what? What is man's limit? Man's limit is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. Whoever exceeds his limit and does not worship Allah, he is the transgressor. This is the transgressor, because he has overstepped the limit. You were not created to eat, enjoy yourself, and take pleasure as livestock do. You were created to worship Allah, so worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you do not, then you have transgressed. This is transgression: that a person does not worship Allah.

His saying ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ and the previous attribute are mutually connected. The one who transgresses against the worship of Allah prefers the worldly life, because he uses it as an excuse to abandon obedience to Allah and is distracted by it from obeying Allah. When the dawn call is made, he prefers sleep over prayer. When he is told to remember Allah, he prefers idle talk over the remembrance of Allah, and so on.

His saying ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ means: it will be his abode. "Refuge" (ma'wā) means the place of return and the dwelling. How wretched is the dwelling of Hellfire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40] means: he feared standing before Him, because on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will confront a person with his sins, and he will say: "I did such and such, I did such and such, I did such and such," as occurs in the authentic hadith. When he confesses, Allah will say to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you."[1] This is the one who feared this standing.

﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40]: that is, from its desires. The soul commands evil, and it commands only wrongdoing. But there is another soul opposed to it, the tranquil soul, because a human being has three souls: the tranquil soul, the commanding soul, and the self-reproaching soul, and all are mentioned in the Qur'an.

As for the tranquil soul, it is in His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise﴾ [Al-Fajr 27–30].

As for the commanding soul to evil, it is in His saying: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent commander of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

As for the self-reproaching soul, it is in His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 1–2].

A person senses these souls within himself. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward good, he loves good and does it; this is the tranquil soul. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward evil and does it; this is the commanding soul to evil. Then comes the self-reproaching soul, which blames him for what he did, so you find him regretting the sin he committed. Or there is another self-reproaching soul that blames him for doing good, may Allah protect us. Some people may blame themselves for doing good and for keeping company with the people of good, and say: "How can I keep company with these people who have turned me away from my life, my desires, my amusements, and the like?"

So the self-reproaching soul is a soul that sometimes blames the commanding soul to evil, and sometimes blames the tranquil soul. In reality it is a soul between two souls: it blames the commanding soul when it does evil and causes the person to feel remorse, and it may also blame the tranquil soul when it does good. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40–41]. Paradise is the abode of bliss which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is what the Qur'an says, and the sacred hadith says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[2] This Paradise a person may perceive before he dies. How? When the appointed time arrives and the angels call the soul to depart, they say: "Come out, O tranquil soul, to the pleasure of Allah," and the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [An-Nahl 32]. When do they say it? At the time of death.

So the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise, and its spirit departs content, easy, and smooth. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].

---

[1] Agreed upon (Bukhari 2441; Muslim 2768/52), narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[2] Agreed upon (Bukhari 3244; Muslim 2824/2), narrated from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.
[3] Narrated by al-Bukhari (6507) from 'Ubadah ibn as-Samit, and Muslim (2684/15) from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[4] Narrated in this wording by at-Tirmidhi (2385) from Anas. The hadith is agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3688) and Muslim (2639/161) narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, saying: "When is the Hour?" He said: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "Nothing, except that I love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ." He said: "You are with the one you love." Anas said: "We never rejoiced at anything as we rejoiced at the Prophet's ﷺ saying: 'You are with the one you love.'"

Jibril (may peace be upon him), who is the most knowledgeable of the messengers, asked the Prophet (ﷺ), who is the most knowledgeable of all mankind. He said: "Tell me about the Hour." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "The one who is asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the one who asks" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)]. That is, if it is hidden from you, then it is hidden from me as well. And if the most knowledgeable of the angels and the most knowledgeable of mankind do not know when the Hour will come, then what of those below them? From this we learn that what some people spread, that the Hour will occur on such-and-such a date or in such-and-such a time, is entirely false, and we know that they are liars in this, because they do not know when the Hour will come; none knows it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 45]. That is, you have no knowledge of it, but you are a warner. A warner of whom? ﴿Those who fear it﴾, that is, those who dread it, and they are the believers. As for those who deny it, consider it far-fetched and reject it, warning does not benefit them, ﴿and signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101].

So we say: you do not ask when you will die, nor where you will die, because this is a matter that does not need to be asked about; it is a settled matter, and it must happen. However long you remain in this world, it is as if you remained only a single day. Indeed, as Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46].

But the question that must come to the self, and for which you must have an answer, is: In what state will you die? By my saying "in what state," I do not mean whether you are rich or poor, strong or weak, with a family or childless. No, in what state will you die in terms of your deeds? This is the point.

If you ask yourself this question, you must prepare, you must prepare, because you do not know when death will surprise you. How many a person has gone out driving his car and was brought back carried on shoulders! How many a person has left his family saying, "Prepare lunch or dinner for me," but never ate it! How many a person has put on his shirt and buttoned its buttons, and none undid them except the one who washes him for burial! This is a matter witnessed in sudden accidents, in whatever state one may be.

Look now and think about the state in which you will die—we ask Allah to grant me and you repentance and turning back to Him. Therefore, you should increase your seeking of forgiveness, increase it as much as you can, for seeking forgiveness contains relief from every distress and a way out from every constriction. Some scholars even say: if a person asks you for a fatwa, seek Allah's forgiveness before you issue it, because sins come between a person and guidance. They derived this from the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 105, 106], ﴿that you may judge﴾, ﴿seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 106].

This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes, the day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34–35] is an explanation of this day on which the greatest catastrophe will occur, and it is the day on which man will remember what he strove for. How will he remember it? He will remember it written down, recorded with him, which he himself will read. Allah says: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will encounter spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. When he reads it, he will remember what he strove for, that is, what he did. In this world we have forgotten what we did. We did many deeds, some righteous, some vain, and some evil, but we forget all of this. On the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to us in a book, and it will be said: "Read your record yourself." ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ Then he will remember what he strove for. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I had been dust."﴾ [An-Naba' 40].

Then He said: ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever can see﴾ [An-Nazi'at 36]. May Allah protect us and you from it. ﴿Brought forth﴾ means: made manifest. It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who will lead it. When the wrongdoers are thrown into a narrow place there, bound together, they will call out there for destruction [thubur]. It will come, may Allah protect us, to whoever sees and perceives, and hearts will be torn apart and the infant will turn gray.

For this reason He said: ﴿So as for he who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 37–39]. These are two attributes belonging to the people of the Fire: transgression, which is exceeding the limit, and preferring the life of this world over the Hereafter by giving it precedence over the Hereafter and making it the greatest concern of a person.

If someone asks: what is transgression? We say: transgression is exceeding the limit, as we mentioned just now. Exceeding the limit in what? What is man's limit? Man's limit is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. Whoever exceeds his limit and does not worship Allah, he is the transgressor. This is the transgressor, because he has overstepped the limit. You were not created to eat, enjoy yourself, and take pleasure as livestock do. You were created to worship Allah, so worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you do not, then you have transgressed. This is transgression: that a person does not worship Allah.

His saying ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ and the previous attribute are mutually connected. The one who transgresses against the worship of Allah prefers the worldly life, because he uses it as an excuse to abandon obedience to Allah and is distracted by it from obeying Allah. When the dawn call is made, he prefers sleep over prayer. When he is told to remember Allah, he prefers idle talk over the remembrance of Allah, and so on.

His saying ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ means: it will be his abode. "Refuge" (ma'wā) means the place of return and the dwelling. How wretched is the dwelling of Hellfire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40] means: he feared standing before Him, because on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will confront a person with his sins, and he will say: "I did such and such, I did such and such, I did such and such," as occurs in the authentic hadith. When he confesses, Allah will say to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you."[1] This is the one who feared this standing.

﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40]: that is, from its desires. The soul commands evil, and it commands only wrongdoing. But there is another soul opposed to it, the tranquil soul, because a human being has three souls: the tranquil soul, the commanding soul, and the self-reproaching soul, and all are mentioned in the Qur'an.

As for the tranquil soul, it is in His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise﴾ [Al-Fajr 27–30].

As for the commanding soul to evil, it is in His saying: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent commander of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

As for the self-reproaching soul, it is in His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 1–2].

A person senses these souls within himself. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward good, he loves good and does it; this is the tranquil soul. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward evil and does it; this is the commanding soul to evil. Then comes the self-reproaching soul, which blames him for what he did, so you find him regretting the sin he committed. Or there is another self-reproaching soul that blames him for doing good, may Allah protect us. Some people may blame themselves for doing good and for keeping company with the people of good, and say: "How can I keep company with these people who have turned me away from my life, my desires, my amusements, and the like?"

So the self-reproaching soul is a soul that sometimes blames the commanding soul to evil, and sometimes blames the tranquil soul. In reality it is a soul between two souls: it blames the commanding soul when it does evil and causes the person to feel remorse, and it may also blame the tranquil soul when it does good. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40–41]. Paradise is the abode of bliss which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is what the Qur'an says, and the sacred hadith says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[2] This Paradise a person may perceive before he dies. How? When the appointed time arrives and the angels call the soul to depart, they say: "Come out, O tranquil soul, to the pleasure of Allah," and the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [An-Nahl 32]. When do they say it? At the time of death.

So the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise, and its spirit departs content, easy, and smooth. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].

---

[1] Agreed upon (Bukhari 2441; Muslim 2768/52), narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[2] Agreed upon (Bukhari 3244; Muslim 2824/2), narrated from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.
[3] Narrated by al-Bukhari (6507) from 'Ubadah ibn as-Samit, and Muslim (2684/15) from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.
[4] Narrated in this wording by at-Tirmidhi (2385) from Anas. The hadith is agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3688) and Muslim (2639/161) narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, saying: "When is the Hour?" He said: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "Nothing, except that I love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ." He said: "You are with the one you love." Anas said: "We never rejoiced at anything as we rejoiced at the Prophet's ﷺ saying: 'You are with the one you love.'"

Jibril (may peace be upon him), who is the most knowledgeable of the messengers, asked the Prophet (ﷺ), who is the most knowledgeable of all mankind. He said: "Tell me about the Hour." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "The one who is asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the one who asks" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)]. That is, if it is hidden from you, then it is hidden from me as well. And if the most knowledgeable of the angels and the most knowledgeable of mankind do not know when the Hour will come, then what of those below them? From this we learn that what some people spread, that the Hour will occur on such-and-such a date or in such-and-such a time, is entirely false, and we know that they are liars in this, because they do not know when the Hour will come; none knows it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 45]. That is, you have no knowledge of it, but you are a warner. A warner of whom? ﴿Those who fear it﴾, that is, those who dread it, and they are the believers. As for those who deny it, consider it far-fetched and reject it, warning does not benefit them, ﴿and signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101].

So we say: you do not ask when you will die, nor where you will die, because this is a matter that does not need to be asked about; it is a settled matter, and it must happen. However long you remain in this world, it is as if you remained only a single day. Indeed, as Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46].

But the question that must come to the self, and for which you must have an answer, is: In what state will you die? By my saying "in what state," I do not mean whether you are rich or poor, strong or weak, with a family or childless. No, in what state will you die in terms of your deeds? This is the point.

If you ask yourself this question, you must prepare, you must prepare, because you do not know when death will surprise you. How many a person has gone out driving his car and was brought back carried on shoulders! How many a person has left his family saying, "Prepare lunch or dinner for me," but never ate it! How many a person has put on his shirt and buttoned its buttons, and none undid them except the one who washes him for burial! This is a matter witnessed in sudden accidents, in whatever state one may be.

Look now and think about the state in which you will die—we ask Allah to grant me and you repentance and turning back to Him. Therefore, you should increase your seeking of forgiveness, increase it as much as you can, for seeking forgiveness contains relief from every distress and a way out from every constriction. Some scholars even say: if a person asks you for a fatwa, seek Allah's forgiveness before you issue it, because sins come between a person and guidance. They derived this from the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 105, 106], ﴿that you may judge﴾, ﴿seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 106].

This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 79, verses 27–46 (part 1 of 2)**

Held every Thursday. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make these gatherings blessed. We begin this session with the explanation (tafsir) of verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We started from Surah An-Naba' and are proceeding to the end of the Qur'an. We are now at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He built it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 27–28], and so on to the end.

Allah, glorified and exalted, addresses His servants, saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾. By this interrogative He intends to establish that resurrection is possible, because the polytheists denied the Prophet ﷺ regarding resurrection and said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 78]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾

The answer is known to everyone: it is the heaven, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir 57].

﴿He built it﴾: this sentence is not connected to what precedes it. Therefore, when the reader recites, he should pause at His saying ﴿or is the heaven?﴾, then begin anew with ﴿He built it﴾. The sentence is resumptive (istinafiyyah, a new sentence), to show the greatness of the heaven.

﴿He built it﴾ means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, built it. In another verse, in Surah Adh-Dhariyat, Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that He built it with power, as He said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength [bi-aydin], and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 47]. ﴿With strength﴾ means: with might.

﴿He raised its height and proportioned it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 28]: ﴿raised its height﴾ means: He raised it above the earth. He raised it, the Mighty and Majestic, without pillars, as He said: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you see﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 2].

﴿And proportioned it﴾ means: He made it level and made it complete and perfect, as He said regarding the creation of man: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you and proportioned you﴾ [Al-Infitar 6–7]. That is, He made you well-formed and of complete creation. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, proportioned the heaven.

﴿And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness﴾ [An-Nazi'at 29]: ﴿He darkened its night﴾ means: He made it dark, so the night is dark. Allah says: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra' 12].

﴿And extracted its brightness﴾: He explained it by the sun, which rises each day from its place of rising and sets in its place of setting.

﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 30]: ﴿after that﴾ means: after the creation of the heavens and the earth.

﴿He spread it out﴾, and He explained this spreading by His saying: ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾ [An-Nazi'at 31–32], ﴿as enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾ [An-Nazi'at 33]. The earth was created before the heaven, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed firmly on it mountains from above it, and blessed it, and determined in it its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat 9–12]. So the earth was created before the heaven, but its spreading out, the extraction of water from it, and its pasture came after the creation of the heavens.

﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾: that is, He made them fixed in the earth, holding the earth so that it would not shake with its creatures.

﴿As enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾: that is, Allah, exalted is He, made that as enjoyment for us, which we use for what we eat and drink, and for our livestock, that is, our animals: camels, cattle, sheep, and others.

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminded His servants of these blessings, which indicate the perfection of His power, He reminded them of their inevitable end, which none can avoid. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34]. That is the establishment of the Hour. He called it "catastrophe" (ṭāmmah) because it is a great calamity that overwhelms everything before it. "Greatest" (kubrā) means: greater than every other catastrophe.

﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes, the day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34–35] is an explanation of this day on which the greatest catastrophe will occur, and it is the day on which man will remember what he strove for. How will he remember it? He will remember it written down, recorded with him, which he himself will read. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. When he reads it, he will remember what he strove for, that is, what he did. In this world we have forgotten what we did. We did many deeds, some righteous, some vain, and some evil, but we forget all of this. On the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to us in a book, and it will be said: "Read your record yourself." ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ Then he will remember what he strove for. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I had been dust."﴾ [An-Naba' 40].

Then He said: ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever can see﴾ [An-Nazi'at 36]. May Allah protect us and you from it. ﴿Brought forth﴾ means: made manifest. It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who will lead it. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 45]. That is, you have no knowledge of it, but you are a warner. However long you remain in this world, it is as if you remained only a single day. Indeed, as Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46].

But the question that must come to the self, and for which you must have an answer, is: In what state will you die? By my saying "in what state," I do not mean whether you are rich or poor, strong or weak, with a family or childless. No, in what state will you die in terms of your deeds? This is the point.

If you ask yourself this question, you must prepare, you must prepare, because you do not know when death will surprise you. How many a person has gone out driving his car and was brought back carried on shoulders! How many a person has left his family saying, "Prepare lunch or dinner for me," but never ate it! How many a person has put on his shirt and buttoned its buttons, and none undid them except the one who washes him for burial! This is a matter witnessed in sudden accidents, in whatever state one may be.

Look now and think about the state in which you will die—we ask Allah to grant me and you repentance and turning back to Him. Therefore, you should increase your seeking of forgiveness, increase it as much as you can, for seeking forgiveness contains relief from every distress and a way out from every constriction. Some scholars even say: if a person asks you for a fatwa, seek Allah's forgiveness before you issue it, because sins come between a person and guidance. They derived this from the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 105, 106], ﴿that you may judge﴾, ﴿seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 106].

This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 79, verses 27–46 (part 1 of 2)**

Held every Thursday. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make these gatherings blessed. We begin this session with the explanation (tafsir) of verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We started from Surah An-Naba' and are proceeding to the end of the Qur'an. We are now at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He built it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 27–28], and so on to the end.

Allah, glorified and exalted, addresses His servants, saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾. By this interrogative He intends to establish that resurrection is possible, because the polytheists denied the Prophet ﷺ regarding resurrection and said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin 78]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾

The answer is known to everyone: it is the heaven, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir 57].

﴿He built it﴾: this sentence is not connected to what precedes it. Therefore, when the reader recites, he should pause at His saying ﴿or is the heaven?﴾, then begin anew with ﴿He built it﴾. The sentence is resumptive (istinafiyyah, a new sentence), to show the greatness of the heaven.

﴿He built it﴾ means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, built it. In another verse, in Surah Adh-Dhariyat, Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that He built it with power, as He said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength [bi-aydin], and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 47]. ﴿With strength﴾ means: with might.

﴿He raised its height and proportioned it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 28]: ﴿raised its height﴾ means: He raised it above the earth. He raised it, the Mighty and Majestic, without pillars, as He said: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you see﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 2].

﴿And proportioned it﴾ means: He made it level and made it complete and perfect, as He said regarding the creation of man: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you and proportioned you﴾ [Al-Infitar 6–7]. That is, He made you well-formed and of complete creation. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, proportioned the heaven.

﴿And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness﴾ [An-Nazi'at 29]: ﴿He darkened its night﴾ means: He made it dark, so the night is dark. Allah says: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra' 12].

﴿And extracted its brightness﴾: He explained it by the sun, which rises each day from its place of rising and sets in its place of setting.

﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [An-Nazi'at 30]: ﴿after that﴾ means: after the creation of the heavens and the earth.

﴿He spread it out﴾, and He explained this spreading by His saying: ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾ [An-Nazi'at 31–32], ﴿as enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾ [An-Nazi'at 33]. The earth was created before the heaven, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed firmly on it mountains from above it, and blessed it, and determined in it its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat 9–12]. So the earth was created before the heaven, but its spreading out, the extraction of water from it, and its pasture came after the creation of the heavens.

﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly﴾: that is, He made them fixed in the earth, holding the earth so that it would not shake with its creatures.

﴿As enjoyment for you and for your livestock﴾: that is, Allah, exalted is He, made that as enjoyment for us, which we use for what we eat and drink, and for our livestock, that is, our animals: camels, cattle, sheep, and others.

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminded His servants of these blessings, which indicate the perfection of His power, He reminded them of their inevitable end, which none can avoid. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34]. That is the establishment of the Hour. He called it "catastrophe" (ṭāmmah) because it is a great calamity that overwhelms everything before it. "Greatest" (kubrā) means: greater than every other catastrophe.

﴿So when the greatest catastrophe comes, the day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [An-Nazi'at 34–35] is an explanation of this day on which the greatest catastrophe will occur, and it is the day on which man will remember what he strove for. How will he remember it? He will remember it written down, recorded with him, which he himself will read. Allah says: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will encounter spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [Al-Isra' 13–14]. When he reads it, he will remember what he strove for, that is, what he did. In this world we have forgotten what we did. We did many deeds, some righteous, some vain, and some evil, but we forget all of this. On the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to us in a book, and it will be said: "Read your record yourself." ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ Then he will remember what he strove for. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I had been dust."﴾ [An-Naba' 40].

Then He said: ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever can see﴾ [An-Nazi'at 36]. May Allah protect us and you from it. ﴿Brought forth﴾ means: made manifest. It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who will lead it. When the wrongdoers are thrown into a narrow place there, bound together, they will call out there for destruction [thubur]. It will come, may Allah protect us, to whoever sees and perceives, and hearts will be torn apart and the infant will turn gray.

For this reason He said: ﴿So as for he who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 37–39]. These are two attributes belonging to the people of the Fire: transgression, which is exceeding the limit, and preferring the life of this world over the Hereafter by giving it precedence over the Hereafter and making it the greatest concern of a person.

If someone asks: what is transgression? We say: transgression is exceeding the limit, as we mentioned just now. Exceeding the limit in what? What is man's limit? Man's limit is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. Whoever exceeds his limit and does not worship Allah, he is the transgressor. This is the transgressor, because he has overstepped the limit. You were not created to eat, enjoy yourself, and take pleasure as livestock do. You were created to worship Allah, so worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you do not, then you have transgressed. This is transgression: that a person does not worship Allah.

His saying ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ and the previous attribute are mutually connected. The one who transgresses against the worship of Allah prefers the worldly life, because he uses it as an excuse to abandon obedience to Allah and is distracted by it from obeying Allah. When the dawn call is made, he prefers sleep over prayer. When he is told to remember Allah, he prefers idle talk over the remembrance of Allah, and so on.

His saying ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ means: it will be his abode. "Refuge" (ma'wā) means the place of return and the dwelling. How wretched is the dwelling of Hellfire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40] means: he feared standing before Him, because on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will confront a person with his sins, and he will say: "I did such and such, I did such and such, I did such and such," as occurs in the authentic hadith. When he confesses, Allah will say to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you."[1] This is the one who feared this standing.

﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40]: that is, from its desires. The soul commands evil, and it commands only wrongdoing. But there is another soul opposed to it, the tranquil soul, because a human being has three souls: the tranquil soul, the commanding soul, and the self-reproaching soul, and all are mentioned in the Qur'an.

As for the tranquil soul, it is in His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise﴾ [Al-Fajr 27–30].

As for the commanding soul to evil, it is in His saying: ﴿And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent commander of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾ [Yusuf 53].

As for the self-reproaching soul, it is in His saying: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 1–2].

A person senses these souls within himself. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward good, he loves good and does it; this is the tranquil soul. Sometimes he finds within himself an inclination toward evil and does it; this is the commanding soul to evil. Then comes the self-reproaching soul, which blames him for what he did, so you find him regretting the sin he committed. Or there is another self-reproaching soul that blames him for doing good, may Allah protect us. Some people may blame themselves for doing good and for keeping company with the people of good, and say: "How can I keep company with these people who have turned me away from my life, my desires, my amusements, and the like?"

So the self-reproaching soul is a soul that sometimes blames the commanding soul to evil, and sometimes blames the tranquil soul. In reality it is a soul between two souls: it blames the commanding soul when it does evil and causes the person to feel remorse, and it may also blame the tranquil soul when it does good. We ask Allah for well-being.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 40–41]. Paradise is the abode of bliss which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prepared for His friends, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. This is what the Qur'an says, and the sacred hadith says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[2] This Paradise a person may perceive before he dies. How? When the appointed time arrives and the angels call the soul to depart, they say: "Come out, O tranquil soul, to the pleasure of Allah," and the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [An-Nahl 32]. When do they say it? At the time of death.

So the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise, and its spirit departs content, easy, and smooth. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, all of us dislike death." He said: "It is not so," meaning: all of us dislike death by natural inclination. "But when the believer is given glad tidings of what is given glad tidings at death, he loves to meet Allah."[3] He loves death and it is easy for him. But when the disbeliever is given glad tidings, may Allah protect us, of what distresses him at death, he dislikes meeting Allah, and his soul flees; it is scattered throughout his body until they pull it out of him, as a skewer is pulled out of wet hair. Wet hair, when a skewer is dragged through it (this is well known among those who card wool), nearly tears it apart from the force of the pulling. Likewise, the soul of the disbeliever, may Allah protect us, is scattered through his body, because it is given glad tidings of punishment and is afraid. For this reason, some people, may Allah protect us, have their faces blackened, though their complexion in life was red. Someone trustworthy told me, and swore to me more than once, and he is among those who wash the dead. He said: "By Allah, two situations passed before me that I will never forget." He said: "I washed two people, but there was time between them." He said: "The face was black and the body was normal. Black, he said, like charcoal, may Allah protect us." I said to him: "I bear witness," because he is given glad tidings of what distresses him, may Allah protect us, and a person who is given glad tidings of what distresses him changes.

So Paradise, O Allah, we ask You that we all be among its people. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. I told you that a person may perceive it before he dies through the glad tidings given to him.

It is not hidden from us what is mentioned in the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, that Anas ibn an-Nadr, I think it was Anas ibn an-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I find the scent of Paradise coming from beyond Uhud." This does not mean an emotional, subjective feeling; it is a real perception. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: some people may perceive the Hereafter while still in this world. Then he set out, fought, and was killed, may Allah be pleased with him.

The conclusion is that Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour, when is its arrival?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 41–42].

﴿They ask you﴾ means: people ask you, as He said in another verse: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ [Al-Ahzab 63]. The people's questioning about the Hour is of two kinds:

First, questioning out of denial and disbelief in it. This is kufr. The polytheists asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour and sought to hasten it. Allah said about them: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [Ash-Shura 18].

Second, questioning about the Hour in order to prepare for it, asking when it will come so that one may get ready. This is not objectionable. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said to him: "What have you prepared for it?" He said: "The love of Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A person is with the one he loves."[4]

People ask the Prophet ﷺ, but their intentions in asking differ. However, whatever their intentions and whatever their questions, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿In what are you [involved] of mentioning it?﴾ [An-Nazi'at 43], meaning that it is not possible for you to mention the Hour to them. Why? Because its knowledge is with Allah, as He said in another verse: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [Al-A'raf 187].

How many a person has put on his shirt and buttoned its buttons, and none undid them except the one who washes him for burial! This is a matter witnessed in sudden accidents, in whatever state one may be.

Look now and think about the state in which you will die—we ask Allah to grant me and you repentance and turning back to Him. Therefore, you should increase your seeking of forgiveness, increase it as much as you can, for seeking forgiveness contains relief from every distress and a way out from every constriction. Some scholars even say: if a person asks you for a fatwa, seek Allah's forgiveness before you issue it, because sins come between a person and guidance. They derived this from the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa' 105, 106], ﴿that you may judge﴾, ﴿seek forgiveness of Allah﴾, ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 106].

This is a good inference, and it can also be derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Seeking forgiveness is a safeguard of guidance. Therefore, I advise myself and you to be vigilant, to seek forgiveness often, and to take account of the self, so that we may be fully prepared for the death that we fear may surprise us—we ask Allah to grant us and you a good end.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning thereof, when they see it﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. That is, when they see the Resurrection. ﴿Had not remained but an evening or a morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. The "'ashiyyah" (evening) is from the decline of the sun until its setting, and the "duha" (morning) is from the rising of the sun until its decline. That is, it is as if they remained only half a day. And this is the reality. If I asked you now: how have the years that have passed felt to you? Do you feel now that they were years, or as if it was one day? As if it was one day, without doubt. A person now stands between three things: a day that has passed, which he has lost; a future day, of which he does not know whether he will reach it or not; and the present moment, which is the thing for which he is responsible. As for what has passed, it is gone, and what is gone is gone. What has passed has departed from you. As for the future, you do not know whether you will reach it, and the present is what you are responsible for.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant me and you a good outcome, and to make our end praiseworthy and our final state happy; indeed He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.
